Appendix I Conditional-Mean Diagnostics

Residual-correction test.

This appendix tests on three large external corpora, separately from our benchmarks. The proposition is a population statement, and finite networks need not be unbiased. For a frozen fitted predictor and Rt=Yt−μ^​(Xt)R_{t}=Y_{t}-\widehat{\mu}(X_{t}), the projection identity gives

supc𝔼​‖Rt‖2−𝔼​‖Rt−c⁡(Xt)‖2𝔼​‖Rt‖2=𝔼​‖𝔼⁡[Rt∣Xt]‖2𝔼​‖Rt‖2,\sup_{c}\frac{\mathbb{E}\|R_{t}\|^{2}-\mathbb{E}\|R_{t}-c(X_{t})\|^{2}}{\mathbb{E}\|R_{t}\|^{2}}=\frac{\mathbb{E}\|\mathbb{E}[R_{t}\mid X_{t}]\|^{2}}{\mathbb{E}\|R_{t}\|^{2}}, (66)

so a held-out correction cc that reduces residual energy detects a violation. The five cells use DINOv2-S on AntMaze, HumanoidMaze and PushT, and V-JEPA 2 on AntMaze and HumanoidMaze. The test uses unweighted squared-loss predictors and disjoint fitting and report episodes.

Predictor fitting.

We freeze DINOv2-S or V-JEPA 2, discard any pretraining predictor, and fit a fresh squared-loss mean head on the official OGBench [42] AntMaze/HumanoidMaze stitch corpora; a matched DINOv2 experiment uses the large PushT corpus. OGBench predictors receive four past frames as context and predict only f⁡(Ot+1)f(O_{t+1}) from that context and AtA_{t}; PushT uses its checkpoint-compatible five-control macro-action. AntMaze, HumanoidMaze, and PushT provide respectively 985k, 1.985M, and 1.441M episode-valid training windows.

DINOv2-S uses vit_small_patch14_dinov2 at 224 pixels.

V-JEPA 2 uses facebook/vjepa2-vitl-fpc64-256 with repeated-frame self-clips.

Humanoid/DINOv2 retains a 2×22\times 2 patch grid; the other image features are globally pooled. PushT/DINOv2 uses 16 context frames and five concatenated controls per macro-step. OGBench uses the official visual stitch corpora, stitch-val report episodes and registered third-person camera; PushT uses push-t.lance, reserving 20% of its training split for validation after the 80% train split. The action-concatenating MLP uses SiLU, LayerNorm and three width-1,024 hidden layers (two for maze V-JEPA 2). AdamW uses zero weight decay, gradient clipping at 1 and bfloat16 precision. Linear warmup spans 5% of the stage (0.5% for final temporal PushT stages), followed by cosine decay to 1% of the peak learning rate. Maze DINOv2 and V-JEPA 2 use peak rate 3×10−43\times 10^{-4} and batch/device 32/16 (AntMaze/Humanoid DINOv2) or 8 (V-JEPA 2); PushT/DINOv2 uses 3×10−53\times 10^{-5} and batch/device 2. Final-stage budgets are one epoch and can resume earlier fits. Training uses stable-pretraining, like the benchmark predictors; seeds and the exact training history accompany the code release.

Test information and uncertainty.

Write XX for the frozen information supplied to each world model. Holding the fitted model fixed, we train a separate linear correction and a two-layer, 2048-wide MLP to predict its residual R=Y−μ^​(X)R=Y-\widehat{\mu}(X) on one set of episodes, then measure the fraction ϕ\phi of residual energy removed on disjoint episodes. By (), the unrestricted optimum is the normalized energy in 𝔼⁡[R∣X]\mathbb{E}[R\mid X]; the achieved MLP gain is a lower bound on that quantity and hence a powered falsification test, not a proof of the unrestricted moment. We predeclare a 1% correction margin, cluster-bootstrap whole episodes, and use one-sided 99% upper bounds for a Bonferroni family-wise 95% statement over the five environment–encoder cells. Deterministic XX-dependent errors injected at 0.5%, 1%, and 2% calibrate the procedure’s power (, right). No cell admits a correction above the margin ().

Distribution shift.

The primary PushT predictor admits an 18.92%18.92\% correction on a chronologically held-out block with shifted simulator-state occupancy. The primary inference therefore concerns the matched behavior-data support.

Patch-grid check.

As a supplementary representation check, we repeat the DINOv2 tests while retaining a ×44\!\times\!4 grid of patch tokens (6,144 target coordinates) instead of global pooling. The same correction procedure remains nonpositive on AntMaze (−.0145%-.0145\%, 95% CI [−.0202,−.0090]%[-.0202,-.0090]\%) and HumanoidMaze (−.0159%-.0159\%, 95% CI [−.0196,−.0123]%[-.0196,-.0123]\%), over 302.6M and 609.8M scalar residuals, respectively. This supplementary check is outside the five-cell family-wise claim.

Appendix J Teaser Setup

is an illustrative toy, not one of our benchmarks: a boat picks its heading a′a^{\prime} and moves one boat length through water that drifts it. The hidden current is an east-west mean flow plus eddies: a random divergence-free field, the sum of three waves 1010 to 2020 boat lengths long whose pattern drifts slowly in time, drawn anew for every episode. The boat moves through the water while the water moves it, so the drift depends slightly on where the boat goes. The top panel plots the distance to the center of the view after the move and the bottom panel the drift off heading, i.e., the course over ground minus the heading. Gray points are every possible future from the same state, 300300 currents from the training law for each of 2121 headings, every 18∘18^{\circ} (column width: outcome density). Where the mean flow and the eddies align, the current nears the boat’s speed and can turn its course by up to 180∘180^{\circ}, so the bottom panel shows the curves and the central 99%99\% of the gray points; the diamond is the one observed outcome, at the executed heading ata_{t}, also marked on the heading axis; the frames are the same crop of 224224-pixel images. The left and top-right frames are the two model inputs. The bottom-right frame is the true counterfactual for heading −126∘-126^{\circ} under the same current, rendered by the function that produced the model inputs, which reproduces the observed frame exactly; no model sees it. Arrows and outlines are drawn over the frames and leave their pixels unchanged. Each arrow is the drift the current causes at its location over the transition, and each outline draws the rendered hull, with heading −126∘-126^{\circ}, at the position a model predicts. This heading is roughly opposite the executed one, and both models’ position errors there are close to their medians over the 8181 headings of the curves, every 4.5∘4.5^{\circ} (0.520.52 and 0.140.14 boat lengths, against medians of 0.470.47 and 0.140.14). The JEPA uses frozen MAE features; the counterfactual world model adds the observed minus predicted position to its prediction, the exact correction for a uniform current and an approximate one under eddies. Its median error is 0.080.08 against 0.240.24 boat lengths and 3.1∘3.1^{\circ} against 17.6∘17.6^{\circ}, and over 10001000 fresh events the drift R2R^{2} is 77%77\% against −7%-7\%. The event, the 80th percentile of mean-flow strength among 3232, was chosen from the simulator before any prediction was computed.

J.1  Current Field Ablation

The ablation of keeps the boat, the mean flow and the eddy speed of the title page and changes one property of the eddies at a time. Each of the three waves has a wavelength drawn uniformly in [L,2​L][L,2L] boat lengths and a phase that drifts at a rate drawn uniformly between minus and plus the stated phase rate; the title-page current has L=10L=10 and phase rate 0.30.3. All conditions use the same random draws, so changing LL or the phase rate rescales the same fields, and at L=1000L=1000 the eddies are uniform over the region the boat visits. Each condition collects 128128k factual episodes of two transitions and fits on frozen MAE-B features a state readout, a drift head for the realized two-dimensional drift of the current, and two factual predictors with weight decays 10−410^{-4} and 0.30.3, of which it keeps the one with the lower factual validation loss. Each of the 10001000 fresh evaluation events is scored at 1616 alternative headings, every 22.5∘22.5^{\circ}. The oracle predictor without the outcome and residual reuse with exact means use conditional means over 512512 currents from the training law, shared by all headings of an event, and ρ\rho is estimated from the same draws. Relative risks divide the summed squared position error by the summed conditional variance of the position given the source state and heading, which is the risk of the oracle predictor, so this predictor scores one up to Monte Carlo error. The readout recovers the position at 99.96%99.96\% and the east-west drift at 97.597.5–97.9%97.9\%, and factual copying, from the readout or from the true state, stays below 0%0\%, but the north-south drift is recovered at 92.692.6–94.98%94.98\% and the oracle predictor reaches 8686–97%97\% position R2R^{2}, so every condition is diagnostic ().
